title: Separate transfer acceptance from verified completion
summary: A request acknowledgement and a matching destination observation are different evidence.
objectives: Represent pending, unknown and verified outcomes separately.
Avoid turning an uncertain result into a blind retry.

sources.title: HTTP Semantics: idempotent methods
sources.basis: Defines idempotency and limits on automatic retry; this toy model does not implement HTTP semantics.

sections.title: Keep uncertainty visible
paragraphs: A synthetic request starts pending. An acknowledgement records acceptance; it does not prove that the intended bytes reached the destination.
After a timeout, preserve unknown and reconcile the destination before deciding whether retry is safe. An idempotency key is scoped to the operation and payload.

sections.title: Verify the intended result
paragraphs: Only a destination observation bound to the intended content can mark this toy transfer verified. A wrong digest leaves it unverified.
Real adapters also need bounded time, cancellation, scope checks and sanitized errors. Enabling a remote-control server does not supply those product guarantees.

exercise.instruction: Run the selected-knowledge exercises with pnpm test.
exercise.expected: Assert the documented result and its negative boundary; no external operation is performed.

limitations: No network, credentials or remote service are used. The toy model is not a reliable delivery protocol or a production idempotency implementation.
